title: Ask for structured output and check it
outcome: Validate a classifier result before using it.
story: Amina needs a category that the application can use. A paragraph saying “probably a refund” is not the same as a valid, checked category record.

frames.explanation: The application checks an explicit allowed set.
The exercise uses a policy threshold, not a claim that model confidence is calibrated.

sections.title: State a precise task
paragraphs: A useful prompt explains the allowed categories, includes clear examples, and tells the model how to handle ambiguity. Separate application instructions from customer text. Customer text is data and can contain misleading instructions.

Start with an explicit output schema: category is order, refund, or other; confidence is a number from zero to one; no extra fields. Structured output constrains format. It does not prove the category is correct.

sections.title: Validate on the application boundary
paragraphs: Parse the returned JSON, verify the exact fields and allowed values, and reject malformed output. Handle provider refusals, incomplete results, and timeouts as explicit outcomes. Never pass a malformed response into a business operation.

The browser lab uses prepared JSON strings so each failure is reproducible. It does not contact a model. The server workspace has a separate real provider adapter controlled by environment variables and an offline adapter labelled fixture.

sections.title: Keep the provider behind an adapter
paragraphs: An adapter hides provider-specific request details behind a small application interface. The application can ask classify(message) and receive a validated result or a defined failure, while tests supply a fixture adapter.

Keep the API key on the server. Configure a supported model explicitly; do not bake a temporary model choice or key into the frontend. Record prompt, schema, adapter, and model versions with your evaluation result.

sections.title: Treat confidence as a policy signal
paragraphs: This lesson’s threshold is 0.7. It gives practice with a fallback rule; it is not a universal quality threshold. Choose a real threshold using labelled results and the relative costs of wrong routing and human review.

Changing a prompt can change meaning while preserving a schema. Rerun semantic evaluations after prompt, model, or policy changes. A successful schema check is one layer of evidence, followed by quality evaluation.

words.meaning: A definition of the fields and values a result may contain.
A small boundary that translates between your application and a provider.
A provider outcome that does not supply the requested answer.

explanation: Field names, category, and numeric range are checked.
Uncertain or invalid results go to human review.

exercise.title: A classifier boundary
exercise.brief: Write route(raw). Valid JSON must have exactly category and confidence. Return category for confidence >=0.7; otherwise return human. Reject malformed shape, unknown category, and out-of-range confidence.

steps.title: Read a valid record
steps.task: Parse JSON and return its category for the valid examples.

steps.title: Validate the schema
steps.task: Return human for malformed JSON, unknown categories, or extra fields. Confidence must be a finite number in [0,1].
steps.hint: Handle parsing separately from checking fields.

steps.title: Route uncertain cases
steps.task: Return human when confidence is below 0.7. Equality is accepted.
steps.hint: Check the threshold only after the schema is valid.

cases.why: An allowed list limits the result.

cases.why: Extra fields do not become capabilities.

project.title: A replaceable classifier
project.brief: Use the server adapter workspace to classify messages with a validated schema. Test fixtures first, then perform and label a real provider experiment.

milestones.title: Specify output
actions: Write the schema and fallback policy.

milestones.title: Implement the boundary
actions: Test malformed, refused, incomplete, and valid outcomes.
Reject output before routing when validation fails.

milestones.title: Measure meaning
actions: Run labelled messages through the adapter.
Review wrong categories as well as invalid JSON.
Record whether the real provider experiment ran.

acceptance: The application uses one adapter interface.
Provider failures produce a defined fallback.
Semantic results are recorded separately from schema checks.
project.extension: Add a provider timeout and a maximum single retry within the existing budget.
reflection: Which provider outcomes are not ordinary JSON answers?
Why keep semantic evaluation after validation?
